entities.summary: Sun He (b. 150 CE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, active in Global. He was a key figure in the governance of the Eastern Han dynasty, overseeing military campaigns and administrative reforms. As a prominent leader, Sun He played a crucial role in shaping the fate of the Han dynasty and its successor states. The Han dynasty's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of Confucianism and the Silk Road, which connected China to the wider world. The Han's military campaigns and administrative reforms also had a lasting impact on the development of Chinese bureaucracy and the concept of the 'mandate of heaven'. Sun He's significance lies in his role as a key administrator during a period of significant change and upheaval, and his legacy can be seen in the continued relevance of Han-era institutions and policies in modern China.
